_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Andorra covering Charlemagne legend (founding 788), Paréage treaty 1278 (dual sovereignty French/Spanish bishops), medieval Pyrenean microstate, feudal co-principality survived to present, 1993 constitutional modernisation, tax haven, ski tourism, and unique dual head-of-state system.

country_profile.currency: Euro (EUR, not EU member but uses euro by agreement)

religion.note: Overwhelmingly Catholic (Catalan/Spanish/French heritage); Catholicism not state religion since 1993 constitution but deeply embedded; Our Lady of Meritxell patron saint

ethnic_groups.name: Andorran
ethnic_groups.notes: Catalan-speaking native Andorrans; minority in own country due to immigration; Catalan cultural identity

ethnic_groups.name: Spanish
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest foreign community; workers in tourism/construction

independence.from: Paréage treaty (feudal agreement between Bishop of Urgell and Count of Foix, now French President)

country_profile.notes_unique: Only country with Catalan as sole official language; world's only co-principality (French President + Bishop of Urgell as co-princes); Paréage 1278 (oldest continuous feudal agreement); no military (France/Spain defend); tax haven (no income tax until 2015); ski tourism (~8M visitors/year vs 80k population); highest capital in Europe (1,023m); Andorrans minority in own country (~48%); oldest parliament in Pyrenees (Consell General since 1419); never formally part of EU; oldest state in Europe by some reckonings

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.title: Cap de Govern (Head of Government)

920.name: Paréage and Co-Principality Established
920.description: The landmark Paréages of 1278 and 1288 that established Andorra's unique co-principality under the joint sovereignty of the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix.

sub_clusters.description: The two Paréage treaties that created the constitutional framework of Andorran co-sovereignty, alternating jurisdiction, and tribute obligations that persist to this day.

940.name: Napoleonic Disruption and Restoration
940.description: Napoleon's renunciation and restoration of co-princely authority, the principality's near-absorption into France, and Andorra's survival as a feudal anachronism through the 19th century.

sub_clusters.name: French Revolution and Napoleonic Era
sub_clusters.description: The French Revolution's rejection of feudal titles briefly suspended the co-principality; Napoleon restored the arrangement in 1806 at the Andorrans' request, preserving the unique constitutional structure.
key_events: Napoleon restores French co-princely sovereignty over Andorra at Andorran petition (1806)
